title: Bare HH:MM:SS in front matter silently becomes an integer (YAML 1.1 sexagesimal)

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Found reviewing kanbus-dacb70. PRE-EXISTING PyYAML behavior, not introduced by that fix, but it defeats part of it.

REPRO:
  front matter:  t: 13:30:00
  markus ast ->  "t": 48600

CAUSE: PyYAML implements YAML 1.1, where bare HH:MM:SS is a SEXAGESIMAL INTEGER literal, not a time. 13*3600 + 30*60 = 48600. The value is converted to a meaningless int by the YAML loader BEFORE any Markus code sees it.

TWO CONSEQUENCES:
1. SILENT DATA CORRUPTION. A publication time in front matter becomes a nonsense integer with no error at all. This is the exact failure class kanbus-dacb70 was told to avoid - it is arguably worse than the crash that bug fixed, because it is silent. Newsroom content has publication times; this will bite.
2. The datetime.time branch of _to_json_safe added in kanbus-dacb70 (e374323) is effectively DEAD CODE for YAML front matter, since PyYAML never produces a datetime.time from a bare HH:MM:SS. Worth confirming and either removing it or making it reachable.

NOTE date is unaffected: 'when: 2026-09-04' correctly yields datetime.date and now serializes to ISO 8601. Only bare times are affected.

FIX DIRECTIONS (decide deliberately, this is a contract question):
(a) Use a YAML 1.2 core-schema loader (e.g. ruamel.yaml in 1.2 mode), where sexagesimals are gone and 13:30:00 stays a string. Cleanest semantics; check blast radius on existing front matter.
(b) Keep PyYAML but install a resolver that removes the sexagesimal int pattern.
(c) Document that times must be quoted, and detect the ambiguous pattern to raise a clear error rather than silently coercing.

(a) or (b) preferred - option (c) still relies on authors remembering. Whatever is chosen, add behave coverage.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED option (b): kept PyYAML, patched a custom `FrontMatterLoader(yaml.SafeLoader)` in `src/markusmd/_frontmatter_yaml.py` that removes only the sexagesimal alternative from the int/float implicit resolvers. `parse.py::_split_front_matter` now uses `yaml.load(raw, Loader=FrontMatterLoader)` instead of `yaml.safe_load`.

REPRO (before): `t: 13:30:00` -> `"t": 48600`.
REPRO (after): `t: 13:30:00` -> `"t": "13:30:00"`. Also confirmed `13:30:00.500` (sexagesimal float) -> stays the string `"13:30:00.500"`.

BLAST RADIUS investigated directly against the patched loader (not assumed):
- octal `0755` -> still int 493 (unchanged)
- hex `0x1F` -> still int 31 (unchanged)
- binary `0b101` -> still int 5 (unchanged)
- decimal `42` -> still int 42 (unchanged)
- float `3.14`, `.inf`, `.nan` -> unchanged
- bool forms `yes/no/on/off/true` -> still bool (unchanged)
- bare `y`/`n` -> still string (unchanged, PyYAML never treated single-char y/n as bool anyway)
- `date: 2026-09-04` -> still `datetime.date` (unchanged); `published_at: 2026-09-04T12:30:00` -> still `datetime.datetime` (unchanged)
Only sexagesimal-shaped scalars change type. Nothing else in PyYAML's YAML-1.1 resolution moves.

WHY NOT (a) ruamel.yaml 1.2 core schema: verified via the actual regex semantics that switching schemas would ALSO change existing-content behavior beyond the reported bug -- YAML 1.2 core schema drops `yes/no/on/off/y/n` as booleans (only true/True/TRUE/false/False/FALSE survive) and drops YAML-1.1 octal (`0755` becomes a plain string in 1.2 core schema; only `0o755` is octal). That is a second silent-type-change surface, just less likely to be hit today than the sexagesimal bug -- exactly the failure class this contract is trying to avoid, plus it adds a new runtime dependency (ruamel.yaml) not currently in pyproject.toml. Option (b) has zero blast radius outside the one reported pattern and adds no dependency, so I implemented it.

`datetime.time` branch (kanbus-dacb70 / commit e374323): CONFIRMED dead for the YAML front-matter pipeline, independent of this fix. PyYAML's own `construct_yaml_timestamp` regex requires a full `YYYY-MM-DD` before it will even look for a time component -- forcing `!!timestamp 13:30:00` throws inside PyYAML itself (`'NoneType' object has no attribute 'groupdict'`), so no spelling of front matter ever produces a bare `datetime.time`. Since `Document.front_matter` is a public `Any`-typed dict, the branch was theoretically reachable via hand-constructing a `Document` outside the YAML pipeline, but nothing in this codebase (production or behave suite) does that, and it had zero test coverage. Removed `datetime.time` from `_TEMPORAL_TYPES` in `src/markusmd/ast.py`; a hand-built `Document` with a raw `datetime.time` in front matter now raises `MarkusSerializationError` naming the type, consistent with how `!!set`/`!!binary` are already handled (explicit failure over silent/undocumented special-casing). Docstrings on `Document.to_dict` and `_to_json_safe` updated to explain why.

VERIFICATION:
- `markus ast /tmp/fm.md` after fix: `{"t": "13:30:00"}` (was `{"t": 48600}` before).
- `behave`: 8 features passed, 168 scenarios passed, 885 steps passed, 0 failed (baseline before this change: 163 scenarios / 867 steps, all passing -- added 5 new scenarios / 18 new steps covering the fix and the blast-radius cases above).
- `ruff check src features`: All checks passed.
- Regression guard: `markus convert` output byte-identical (md5-compared) before/after for all 4 files: examples/getting-started.md, site/gfm.md, site/gallery.md, site/index.md. `src/markusmd/render.py` untouched (empty diff).
- Versions unchanged at 0.4.0 in both pyproject.toml and src/markusmd/__init__.py.

New file: src/markusmd/_frontmatter_yaml.py (the patched loader). Changed: src/markusmd/parse.py (use it), src/markusmd/ast.py (drop datetime.time), features/front_matter.feature + features/steps/markus_steps.py (new coverage). Committed on feature/document-ir; not pushed, no PR opened. Leaving this issue open for your review per instructions.
